children: The AIB Ireland Services PMI inched up to 55.4 in August 2026 from July’s 55.2, marking the highest reading since November 2025.
The acceleration in services activity was buoyed by a solid increase in new business, boosted by overseas demand, albeit at a more modest pace than in July.
New business accelerated in August, almost matching June’s seven-month high.
Financial services led the sector, followed by technology, media & telecoms. Employment was unchanged, following the fastest rate of job creation in six months in July.
On the price front, input costs rose for the first time in four months, with input price inflation moving further above the long-run survey trend, but remaining the second-weakest in six months.
Meanwhile, output cost inflation accelerated for the first time in four months.
Looking ahead, business sentiment improved to its highest level since February 2025, amid optimism over new business, investment, marketing, planned expansions, and new projects.

title: Irish Services Growth Hits 9-Month High
